data.content_ref: inline:14e084ed5ca7 abstracts from the layer-boundary framing in 2edd20cc5e66: the protocol-level invariant of distinguishability (delivery metadata enabling duplicate detection) subsumes both the writer's safety obligation and the replay layer's idempotency obligation. The distinction between safe and idempotent is not a layer-boundary distinction but a category distinction—operation-level properties versus protocol-level invariants. Under this abstraction, 2edd20cc5e66's claim that 'the log requires safety of its writers' collapses into the weaker requirement that writers attach distinguishing metadata, which 14e084ed5ca7 already grants. This is refuted if distinguishability cannot be enforced independently of writer-level safety—i.e., if attaching delivery metadata that enables downstream deduplication necessarily entails that the writer itself is safe in the operation-level sense, in which case 2edd20cc5e66's layer-boundary framing is irreducible and the category-error claim is itself the error.
